question: A British credit-card statement. Which line decides whether the debt on it ever shrinks?
answer: The minimum payment. Britain's financial regulator counts a cardholder as in persistent debt when, over 18 months, they have paid more in interest and charges than they repaid of what they borrowed. Since 2018 firms must then nudge them, and at 36 months offer a way out. Minimums kept many paying rent on a debt.
move: Compare what a debt costs you with how much it actually shrinks.

scene.body: Balance: £3,000. Minimum payment: £75. If you make only the minimum payment each month, it will take you longer and cost you more to clear your balance.

phrases.why: Balance sounds like money you have. On a card it is the debt.

phrases.plain: Least you can pay to keep the debt alive: £75
phrases.why: At about 2% interest a month, £60 of it is interest. The debt falls by £15.

phrases.plain: it can take you many years
phrases.why: Minimum payments shrink as the debt does, so the end keeps moving away.
